title: Cubic, Reciprocal & Exponential Graphs

problems_fixed.what: Within-tier duplicate answer: this problem (y=2^x at x=3 -> 8) collided with bronze[0] (y=x^3 at x=2 -> 8), literally the same product 2x2x2. Changed x=3 to x=4 so y=16, distinct and still teaching powers of 2.
problems_fixed.old: For y=2^x, find y when x=3 (solution 8)
problems_fixed.new: For y=2^x, find y when x=4 (solution 16)

problems_fixed.what: Within-tier duplicate answer: this problem (y=x^3+1 at x=-1 -> 0) collided with silver[0] (y=x^3-4x at x=2 -> 0). Changed x=-1 to x=-2 so y=-7, distinct and still teaching that a negative cubed stays negative.
problems_fixed.old: For y=x^3+1, find y when x=-1 (solution 0)
problems_fixed.new: For y=x^3+1, find y when x=-2 (solution -7)

solutions_audit: Fresh-solved all 20 bank problems from display text. Every stored solution was already mathematically correct (cubes, reciprocals, powers, the population model 500*2^4=8000, the reciprocal asymptote y=2, and the cubic roots +/-3.46 = +/-sqrt(12)). The only defects were the two within-tier duplicate-answer collisions (a filed disease class). No wrong answers, no degenerate/non-calculator-messy problems found.
opener_concept: Bacteria doubling every hour from 1 (1,2,4,8,...). Inline-SVG exponential curve of count vs hours plotting (0,1),(1,2),(2,4),(3,8),(4,16),(5,32). Student continues the doubling by common sense (16 after 4 h, 32 after 5 h); the reveal names it as the exponential curve y=2^x through (0,1), then introduces the cubic (x^3) and reciprocal (a/x) families the lesson covers.

guided_added.opener: SVG exponential curve + 2 read-off boxes + reveal.
